newsitem.title: USA: Jury selected in Orange County bankruptcy trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury selected in Orange County bankruptcy trial.

text.p: A jury was selected for the trial of former Orange County, Calif., assistant treasurer Matthew Raabe on charges stemming from the county's financial crisis, attorneys said on Wednesday.

The 12-person jury, composed of six men and six women, is expected to begin hearing testimony on March 24. Four alternate jurors were also selected, Deputy Orange County District Attorney Matthew Anderson said.
The trial could last until mid-May, attorneys said.
The county filed for bankruptcy in December 1994 after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
Raabe was indicted in May 1995 on several counts, including making false statements in the sale of securities and misappropriation of public funds.
Raabe, who has denied any wrongdoing, faces up to 12 years in state prison.
Raabe was one of several Orange County officials to face charges following the bankruptcy.
In April 1995, former county treasurer Robert Citron pleaded guilty to six felonies for his role in the crisis.
A judge last November ordered him to spend a year in jail and pay a $100,000 fine, but Citron was later assigned to a community work program instead of jail.
Last October, a judge sentenced former Orange County budget director Ronald Rubino to probation for charges stemming from the investment crisis.
Meanwhile, the case against county auditor Steven Lewis has been put on hold by a state court pending a decision on his motion to disqualify the district attorney.
